# [TASK] Frontend: debounced live parse-as-you-type wiring

## Task
Wire the frontend search field to live, debounced parse-as-you-type calls.

## Scope
Debounce/race-condition handling only — rendering the highlights themselves
is a separate Task (#209).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Keystrokes debounce (300-500ms of typing pause) before a parse call fires, not one call per keystroke (`Search.test.jsx`'s "collapses rapid typing into a single debounced parseQuery call, not one per keystroke" test)
- [x] A new keystroke while a parse call is in flight cancels/ignores the stale in-flight response when it returns (`Search.test.jsx`'s "discards a stale, out-of-order parseQuery response rather than overwriting newer highlights" test)
- [x] A failed parse call leaves the last valid highlight state in place rather than clearing to an error-looking state (`Search.test.jsx`'s "leaves the last valid highlight spans in place when a parseQuery call fails" test)
- [x] Tests cover rapid typing and out-of-order response arrival (`Search.test.jsx`, describe block "Search - live query highlighting (#208)")

## Estimate
**Hours:** 5

## Notes
Implemented in `Search.jsx` (`handleQueryChange`, a 400ms debounce timer ref, and a `latestParseRef` stale-response guard mirroring the existing `latestQueryRef`), a `parseQuery` mutation in `services/AI.js` hitting #207's endpoint, and `queryHighlightSpans` state in `currentGenreOrCategory.js`. The spans are also cleared by `selectGenreOrCategory`/`searchMovie`/`aiSearchCleared`, so a stale breakdown can't leak into a new search.

A test pins `QUERY_HIGHLIGHT_DEBOUNCE_MS` to AC1's 300-500ms range, so a regression to 0ms would be caught.

No rendering here — `queryHighlightSpans` is stored but not yet consumed. That's #209 and #210.
